title: Time Jump: 08:45 Wednesday, Oil Past the Intakes

fields.narration: We are moving forward a full day. It is now 08:45 Central Daylight Time on Wednesday 9 June 2027, about 27 hours since the Prairie Line was shut in. Overnight, the leading edge of the slick passed mile 34, inside the TRJ-02 window. The line is still shut in, and Mill Ridge Station and Sandhill Valve are still closed. Through the night, Prairie Spill's deflection stations at miles 9.5, 28, 31 and 33 pushed oil into the recovery pockets on the bank. Six portable tanks at the Mill Ridge staging area are now full of oily liquid. The river has not changed: about 8,500 cubic feet per second, moving at about 2 knots. The overnight reports say the leading edge is past all intakes. The rural water district is still buying water through the interconnect. Sterling Bluff is still running on storage and wells. The questions on the table now are what comes back first, and who decides.
worldState: Clock: 08:45 CDT, Wednesday 9 June 2027. About 27 hours since the 06:04 shutdown.
The Prairie Line is still shut in. Mill Ridge Station (MP 213.1) and Sandhill Valve (MP 215.6) are still CLOSED.
Release estimate is unchanged: 2,700–3,500 bbl of medium sour crude. Planning figure 3,100 bbl. Basis: SCADA volume balance VB-0620. Still UNVERIFIED. Cause is unknown.
The leading edge passed the Prairie Bend RWD intake (mile 11) and the Sterling Bluff WD intake (mile 34) overnight, inside the TRJ-02 windows. Trailing oil and sheen may still be in the river.
Deflection boom at miles 9.5, 28, 31 and 33 ran overnight, sending oil into recovery pockets on the bank.
Mill Ridge staging area: six 500-bbl portable tanks are full of recovered oily liquid. This is an oil-and-water mixture, not a recovered-oil figure. The oil fraction has not been measured.
Kansas River: about 8,500 cfs, surface velocity about 2.3 mph (2 knots), with no significant change in flow.
The Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks closure of the Mill Ridge boat ramp and Kaw Valley Fishing Access is still in effect.
The Prairie Bend RWD intake at mile 11 is closed. The district has been buying water from Sterling Bluff through the interconnect since Tuesday afternoon.
The Sterling Bluff WD intake gate has been closed since Tuesday. The city is running on storage and wells, and the storage clock is still counting down.
Overnight reports: the leading edge is past all intakes. Nobody has issued a reopening order or proposal; trailing oil and sheen are still being reported.
JIC: the public line (555-0118) is down to 19 calls in queue. The claims line (555-0131) is now announced and ringing steadily.
fields.facilitatorNote: Let the room take in the new baseline before taking questions. If players start talking about reopening, ask who closed the ramp and who closed each intake. Push the Environmental Unit on what data it has, as of this morning, to support pulling boom.
fields.scenarioTitle: Ditch to Intake — Prairie Line River Crossing Release & Water Intakes

instructorNote: This card resets the baseline for the reopening phase. Watch whether the QI and IC hold that reopening is not theirs to order. KDWP decides when the ramp and fishing access reopen, and each utility decides on its own intake using the Environmental Unit's recommendation, the state's input and its own sampling. Also watch whether ENVL asks for a trajectory rerun and post-passage sampling before anyone agrees to demobilize boom.
